problems.stem: For the Module 6 studio submission, you must deliver a complete published portfolio. Which file tree is ready to publish as a GitHub Pages user site?
options: A single page.html with all content and no stylesheet or images
index.html, about.html, projects/index.html, resume.pdf, and assets/style.css committed to the username.github.io repo
A Word document exported as portfolio.docx
A folder of screenshots of what the site would look like
problems.explanation: A publishable studio deliverable is the actual file tree (lowercase index.html, linked pages, assets) committed to the correctly named repo, not a mockup or a document.

problems.stem: Your studio checklist covers accessibility, privacy, and publishing. Which combination shows you applied all three module skills?
options: Bright colors, autoplay music, and a hit counter
Alt text on every image, no API keys or personal data in the repo, and a working live URL verified on another device
A long About page with no images and no links
A single commit message that says done
problems.explanation: The module integrates accessibility (alt text), privacy (no secrets or personal data committed), and publishing (a verified live URL). All three together signal mastery.

problems.stem: You used an AI assistant (for example GitHub Copilot, Claude, or ChatGPT) to draft your HTML, debug a CSS issue, and reword a resume bullet. What does the module ask you to include so the work is honest?
options: Nothing; AI use never needs to be mentioned
A short AI-use note stating where AI helped (drafting, debugging, wording) and confirming you verified the output and own the final decisions
A claim that you wrote everything yourself
The full chat transcript pasted into the home page
problems.explanation: The module's standard is a concise AI-use note that discloses where AI assisted and affirms you checked the output and remain responsible for the result. Naming the specific tool (and version, if known) and following your course's GenAI disclosure policy makes the note auditable.

problems.stem: Before final submission, which single check best confirms the whole module came together for a real visitor?
options: Open the live username.github.io URL in a private window on a phone and confirm pages load, images show alt text, links work, and no personal secrets are exposed
You spent a lot of hours on it
problems.explanation: A single end-to-end test on the live URL from another device exercises accessibility, publishing, and privacy at once, which is the integrated outcome the studio targets.
